newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrat fears "puppet" leadership after 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK democrat fears "puppet" leadership after 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong's Democratic Party leader Martin Lee appealed to Bejing on Sunday not to install a puppet leader to succeed the British governor when the colony reverts to China in 1997.
Britain hands the colony back to China at midnight on June 30, ending a century and a half of colonial rule.
Beijing has said the person who leads Hong Kong after the handover will be picked by a 400-strong electoral college.

But the pro-democracy camp in Hong Kong has condemned the selection process as unrepresentative and elitist, since the 400 would be chosen by a Chinese-controlled Preparatory Committee, which has the ultimate say in handover affairs.
Lee told government radio that it would benefit both Hong Kong and China if the future leader was not simply a "yes man" kowtowing to Beijing.
"It (would be) like playing a toy car with remote control 2,000 miles away without being able to see the car from the room where you are operating it," he said.
In poll after poll, Chief Secretary Anson Chan, Governor Chris Patten's deputy, has been the hot favourite for the post-1997 leadership.
But her close association with the British administration has been seen as going against her.
Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, tipped as the frontrunner for the chief executive post, has yet to make it clear whether he will stand.
The chief executive will be named in November by the selection committee which will be formed next month.
